basics.name: Tianyu Wu
basics.label: Ph.D. Candidate, Biophysics and Quantitative Biology
basics.summary: Ph.D. candidate at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign working on AI for Biology (AI4Bio) and protein design, with a focus on automatic scientific discovery: building generative AI systems that propose scientific hypotheses and designs. Background in AI for protein engineering, focused on physicochemical properties such as aggregation propensity, with applications including Rubisco engineering.

work.name: Luthey-Schulten Group, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
work.summary: Spatially resolved whole-cell simulation of baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).
highlights: Built the first 4D hybrid RDME-ODE simulations of the yeast galactose switch on the GPU-based Lattice Microbes platform, with cell geometry taken from cryo-electron tomograms.
Benchmarked the multi-GPU solver under different spatial decompositions.
Platform talk and session co-chair, Systems Biophysics, Biophysical Society Annual Meeting 2026.

work.name: Diwakar Shukla Group, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
work.position: Graduate Researcher, AI for Biology and Protein Design
work.summary: Generative AI systems that propose scientific hypotheses and designs.
highlights: Learned ranker for protein-ligand pose prediction that reaches 86.0% top-1 accuracy on PoseBusters v2.
Protein language models (ESM2) adapted with LoRA fine-tuning.
Tests of whether LLM representations and outputs can be trusted, using acceptance guards and null controls (NeurIPS 2026 XAI4Science workshop).
Methods for automatic scientific discovery: deciding which measurement separates competing mechanistic explanations of the same data.

projects.name: Computational Protein Engineering: Form II Rubisco (Rhodospirillum rubrum)
projects.summary: An end-to-end computational pipeline for engineering a carbon-fixing enzyme, from predictive models to designs a collaborating wet lab can test.
highlights: Trained and benchmarked sequence- and structure-based models on deep mutational scanning data; established calibration and error floors before using predictions to rank candidates.
Ran molecular dynamics, free-energy, and quantum-chemical calculations on the catalytic site; built decoy and radial controls to test whether a proposed structural descriptor is actually site-local.

Designed de novo binders and redesigned active sites with generative backbone models; converted the surviving designs into ordered constructs, matched controls, and assay protocols for experimental validation.

projects.name: Predicting Protein Aggregation Propensity with Protein Language Models
projects.summary: A sequence-based machine-learning framework for aggregation propensity, from whole-protein prediction to residue-level aggregation-prone regions. First-author manuscript in preparation.
highlights: Built a protein language model-based predictor of aggregation propensity, trained on a published high-throughput stability library and extended to residue-level aggregation-prone region detection.
Designed nested and external validation protocols; benchmarked against public curated aggregation databases and training-free biophysical baselines.
Ran in-silico deep mutational scanning on an antibody Fab; coordinated experimental validation (DLS, BLI) with collaborators.

highlights: Virtual cell
Single-cell perturbation prediction
